newsitem.title: UK: Mixed picture for Conservatives in Scottish polls.
newsitem.headline: Mixed picture for Conservatives in Scottish polls.

text.p: Support for Britain's ruling Conservatives slumped five points to 12 percent in a Scottish opinion poll published on Wednesday, less than half its 1992 general election level, although a second poll showed their support rising.
In the weekly System Three poll in the Herald newspaper, the Conservatives trail well behind a resurgent Scottish National Party (SNP), up six points to 26 percent and Labour, up one point to 53.
The Liberal Democrats were static at nine percent .
But the Herald poll, conducted by face-to-face interview in 40 of Scotland's 72 constituencies from March 27-30, conflicted with an ICM telephone poll published in the Scotsman newspaper.
This has a three point rise to 20 percent in Conservative support, Labour on 47 and the SNP on 22 percent after the first two weeks of the election campaign.
Conservatives held 10 Scottish seats in the old parliament. Labour had 49, Liberal Democrats nine, and SNP four.
